text:
maria: Heads-up — embeddings from the HF checkpoint we just onboarded are ~12% worse on NQ when run through Redwood. Suspect tokenizer/pooling mismatch, not model weights.

alex: can you paste the conversion steps? iirc we had to set special tokens manually for that repo.

maria: steps: 1) download hf checkpoint 2) convert with `scripts/hf_to_redwood.py` 3) run `redwood-serving --model converted` to get embeddings.

maria: quick config.json we used:
```json
{
  "model_type": "bert",
  "tokenizer_class": "RobertaTokenizer",
  "do_lower_case": false,
  "add_prefix_space": true,
  "cls_token": "<cls>",
  "sep_token": "<sep>"
}
```

kevin: the HF model is actually a RoBERTa-style encoder but with EOS-as-CLS in their repo (they use last token pooling). if your tokenizer defines `<cls>` but the model expects EOS pooling, you get different vectors.

julia: aha. so two axes: (a) pooling: CLS vs EOS vs mean; (b) truncation/padding side + special token insertion. both affect final embeddings.

maria: exact symptoms: on a 384 token truncation we see token counts off by +1 for ~40% of samples. the converted tokenizer shows `cls_token_id`=null in the on-disk vocab but HF's tokenizer had `cls_token_id`=2.

alex: do you have a minimal repro? even a single example where HF and Redwood produce different token ids would help.

maria: repro (python):
```py
from transformers import AutoTokenizer
tok = AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained('local-hf/our-model')
print(tok.encode('What is the capital of France?'))
# -> [0, 887, 5, ... , 2]  # last token is eos/cls per hf
\n# converted redwood tokenizer (on-disk) shows:\n# token ids: [0, 887, 5, ...]  # missing trailing token id
```

eval-bot: perf diff snapshot: baseline HF-meanpool -> P@1 0.72, Redwood-converted -> 0.63 on NQ-200 eval set.

kevin: also watch truncation strategy. HF tokenizer default is `truncation=True, max_length=384, truncation_strategy='longest_first'` and padding side 'right'. If converted tokenizer has `truncation_side='left'` or `pad_to_max_length` behavior changed, the alignment of CLS/EOS moves.

julia: can we check model config attention_mask handling? sometimes we accidentally drop the final token when using `return_tensors='pt'` vs a custom batching path.

maria: i ran a diff on token ids for 1000 samples: 38% had a shifted token after index 0 (prefix issue). so likely `add_prefix_space` mismatch combined with special token mapping.

alex: next steps I propose:
- run token-id diff script (i'll do)
- add a small unit test to `hf_to_redwood.py` to assert `cls_token_id`/`sep_token_id` preserved
- update conversion to fallback to HF tokenizer if ambiguous

maria: also, reranker uses CLS pooling by default in Redwood. the HF repo uses last-token pooling for training. we need a mapping config field like `pooling: last` in model metadata.

kevin: agreed. i'll add `pooling_strategy` to the model manifest and ensure the embedding endpoint applies it. quick patch idea:
```json
"metadata": {
  "pooling_strategy": "last", // options: cls | last | mean
  "truncation_side": "right"
}
```

infra-bot: deploy queued: token-diff-test -> ci (pr #4128).

julia: for quantization experiments - note that int8 or q4/qlora style ops shouldn't affect tokenization but can exacerbate metric drop if pooling index is off (you get different vector entries used). keep quantization separate for now.

maria: i'll attach a tiny sample payload and token diffs to the GH issue. TODOs: @alex run diffs, @julia add manifest field + docs, @kevin add conversion unit test.

alex: on it, starting token-diff run now. will post truncated csv. :mag_right:

maria: thanks — if anyone sees obvious quick wins: unify on `pad_to_max_length=False` and explicit `model_manifest.pooling_strategy`. small docs blurb will save future teams. :thumbsup:
